messages.subject: the alphabet
parts:
I have a local branch that adds a QZ decomposition to the Stan language, but if I call the function QZ it shows up first in the index to the Stan manual instead of at the end of the other functions that start with q. Is there any way to circumvent this or do I need to just name the function qz?

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] the alphabet
parts:
Follow the definition for Phi:

\fitemindexsort{real}{Phi}{real \farg{x}}{
Returns the unit normal cumulative distribution function of \farg{x}.
\[
\mbox{Phi}(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{0}^{x} e^{-t^2/2} dt
\]}{Phi}{phi}

Daniel's guess was spot-on --- the last arg determines the sorting.

- Bob

QZ = Schur decomposition, right? This is a first step towards general evaluation of exp(A*t) to solve ODEs with constant A matrix.

QZ is sometimes called the Generalized Schur decompsition. Regardless of the name, it is just what Eigen does

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/classEigen_1_1RealQZ.html

The remaining bit as far is I recall is evaluating exp(T * t) with T being upper triangular - is this also in the making?

Do you mean T as in the upper-triangular matrix that comes out of the QZ decomposition? If you could point me to a link that explains the connection to ODEs, then maybe I can figure out if this is more useful than I originally intended.

Ben

The thing to do for functions like this is create an issue
on our GitHub tracker with the label "new function":

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues

New functions should have a definition or at least pointers to
references where they're defined. And a description of application
and why it's important (that helps us prioritize).

Is little t a vector or scalar? And I take it exp() is
the matrix exponential, not a pointwise exponential. This
looks like the canonical reference:

http://www.cs.cornell.edu/cv/researchpdf/19ways+.pdf

This relates the matrix exponential to sensitivity analysis
of numerical calcs. It has 1K citations and van Loan is
widely known as the co-author of THE numerical matrix algebra
book, Golub and van Loan.

- Bob

Nope, that's outdated.

See http://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/090768539

This would be really useful to have for continuous time models,
